pr_body:
`EVP_CIPHER` already caches certain constants so that we don't have to query the provider every time. We do the same thing with `EVP_MD` constants. Without this we can get performance issues, e.g. running "speed" with small blocks of data to digest can spend a long time in `EVP_MD_size()`, which should be quick.

Partialy fixes #13578

I've also refactored the `EVP_CIPHER` constant caching to move it into `evp_cipher_from_dispatch`, i.e. to where the `EVP_CIPHER` actually gets constructed rather than where it is fetched in `EVP_CIPHER_fetch`. The problem with the latter is that we construct a cipher once, but we may fetch it many times. We shouldn't have to cache the constants every time we fetch.
pr_comments:
I've run some tests to see the effect on performance of this change. I ran both the "before" and "after" tests with #13721 applied. I'm seeing quite a lot of variability in the results from one run to the next, so my confidence the precise numbers is quite low. To try and reduce variability as much as possible I "warmed up" my machine before both the "before" and "after" tests by repeating the same speed command 5 times and discarding the results. I then ran the command again 5 times and recorded the results.

I compiled with just `config --strict-warnings`, and ran this speed command:

````
openssl speed -evp sha256 -bytes 16
````
The "before" output was:
````
sha256           38566.15k
sha256           36042.71k
sha256           42937.12k
sha256           42312.67k
sha256           44117.60k
````
Which gives an average of 40795.25k

The "after" output was:
````
sha256           46979.81k
sha256           49308.40k
sha256           48095.66k
sha256           46935.39k
sha256           46201.71k
````
Which gives an average of 47504.19k.

This represents a speed-up of approximately 16% (if you believe the numbers).

Deprecated functions like EVP_MD_meth_set_result_size() set md->md_size, which is now the cached value. Either they should actually change something in the provider, return an error, or be removed. This PR doesn't actually introduce the problem, but now seems to use existing variables that were not initialized before, but that we did read and then don't do anything with.

The functions are currently documented to just return 1.
I think it's a separate issue and these functions should not be applicable to provided digests.

> I think it's a separate issue and these functions should not be applicable to provided digests.

Exactly. Those functions are deprecated for a reason. They are intended for use when you are setting up your own custom EVP_MD which you have created yourself.

>  Either they should actually change something in the provider, return an error, or be removed. 

I disagree. They are deprecated and therefore their usage is strongly discouraged. Existing uses will not be broken. I don't see a problem here.

issue_context.title: SHA performance test
comments:
Running the `speed -evp sha256` with 16 and 16384 bytes under valgrind show that for 16-bytes blocks it spends approx. 30% in the `evp_generic_fetch` function (with descendants). For 16384-bytes block this time is about 4%.

So reducing the number of calls of the `evp_generic_fetch` function will significantly improve the difference but I still have questions about how relevant this benchmark is.

Thanks for confirming my suspicions, @beldmit.  In my view, fetching shouldn't be part of the measurement at all, as that's overhead, and because there's a definite "cold" and "hot" state for every algorithm being fetched.

This calls for a bit of refactoring in `apps/speed.c`
Have an option to "prewarm" the fetch or not.  Being able to see the overhead added by the dynamic lookups is useful. And arguably, if you're testing the "EVP" API you want to know all of it :)

> if you're testing the "EVP" API you want to know all of it :)

`openssl speed` is, as far as I know, designed to measure the performance of the algorithms proper.  If you look, you'll find measureing sections formed by `Time_F(START)` and `Time_F(STOP)` timer calls, and will hopefully notice that overhead is outside of the measuring sections.  I can only conclude that some of the overhead has slipped inside those measuring sections.

I am sure it will not be difficult to have the 'speed' program measure how long EVP takes.  I am confident that will be useful, to the project as well.  There is currently no way to understand the overhead right now.

I dived into the `speed` program second time in my life and the impression did not get better since the 1st time.

I think it's worth writing a brand new `speedevp` utility with EVP-only interface inside and deprecate the current `speed` one but don't believe it's realistic for 3.0.

> > if you're testing the "EVP" API you want to know all of it :)
> 
> `openssl speed` is, as far as I know, designed to measure the performance of the algorithms proper. If you look, you'll find measureing sections formed by `Time_F(START)` and `Time_F(STOP)` timer calls, and will hopefully notice that overhead is outside of the measuring sections. I can only conclude that some of the overhead has slipped inside those measuring sections.

We measure speed calling `EVP_Digest` calling `EVP_MD_fetch` calling `evp_generic_fetch`

> We measure speed calling `EVP_Digest` calling `EVP_MD_fetch` calling `evp_generic_fetch`

Ah, yeah, `EVP_Digest()` doesn't lend itself very well for these measurements.  It should probably be divided up in clearer Init/Update/Final steps with appropriate timer start and stop in between.
Wouldn't it be just sufficient to replace EVP_xyz() with an explicit EVP_MD_fetch() outside of the loops?
At least as a dirty hack type of solution.
I've tried it but no, it still invokes EVP_MD_fetch from EVP_DigestInit_ex

Did you really try doing EVP_MD_fetch outside of the loops and not just put the const EVP_shaxyz() call outside of the loops? Because if you use the placeholder EVP_shaxyz() it will cause the implicit EVP_MD_fetch in EVP_DigestIniit_ex to be invoked.  But with an explicitly fetched EVP_MD there should be no implicit fetch in the EVP_DigestInit_ex.

Hmmmmm, I thought that the intention was to detect if the passed md was already fetched (which is easy, there's a `prov` attribute that is non-NULL in that case)...  don't we do that?  That could be worth a dig.

However, hacking inside EVP_Digest_loop doesn't help at all, because this:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/a2e145f8dbf064b56f793fc77b3ccd79f7c67689/apps/speed.c#L2925-L2927

The preparations must happen *outside* of the `Time_F(START)`..`Time_F(STOP)` section!!!

I had an idea that if we provide an explicitly fetched EVP_MD object to EVP_Digest we will not fetch it again and again. If we do it once on the first call instead of once per block, it is not ideal from the benchmark point of view but will give us some clues.

> 
> ```
> diff --git a/apps/speed.c b/apps/speed.c
> index 07c2238ab2..d98f5a59f0 100644
> --- a/apps/speed.c
> +++ b/apps/speed.c
> @@ -1010,6 +1010,9 @@ static int EVP_Digest_loop(void *args)
>      unsigned char md[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE];
>      int count;
>  
> +    if (evp_md == NULL)
> +           evp_md = EVP_MD_fetch(NULL, "sha256", "");
> +
>      for (count = 0; COND(c[D_EVP][testnum]); count++) {
>          if (!EVP_Digest(buf, lengths[testnum], md, NULL, evp_md, NULL))
>              return -1;
> ```

This cannot work because `evp_md != NULL` here but it points at the const, placeholder EVP_MD object for an algorithm.
You would always have to do the explicit fetch here.
```
real_md = EVP_MD_fetch(NULL, OBJ_nid2sn(EVP_MD_type(evp_md)), NULL);
... loop here with real_md ...
EVP_MD_free(real_md);
```

But for quick fix of the -evp option it should be possible to replace the EVP_getdigestbyname() when handling the -evp option with an explicit fetch. Of course it will require changing the evp_md to nonconst and freeing it after the benchmark.

> This cannot work because `evp_md != NULL` here but it points at the const, placeholder EVP_MD object for an algorithm.
> You would always have to do the explicit fetch here.
> 
> ```
> real_md = EVP_MD_fetch(NULL, OBJ_nid2sn(EVP_MD_type(evp_md)), NULL);
> ... loop here with real_md ...
> EVP_MD_free(real_md);
> ```

Yes, it works this way (still with some performance degradation).
For short blocks I suppose that smth from 7% per EVP_MD_size, 7% per EVP_MD_CTX_reset, 7% per EVP_MD_CTX_free, and 7% per ENGINE_get_digest_engine should be eliminated some way.
There are some more issues so reopening.
There are at least 2 PRs to be reviewed and merged.
What I don't understand is why @yxungh  always sees much larger differences.
There was a significant slowdown before #13721 was merged
Isn't this a dup of #13407?

@richsalz, I think it is not because cipher and digest slowdowns are caused by different reasons.

@yxungh, I suppose it can be closed now?
Thanks!

review_comments: Why do we don't check for md here but check in EVP_MD_size?
The same question is about EVP_MD_flags

I'm just reverting the implementation back to the way it used to be in 1.1.1. There, EVP_MD_size() has the check:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/64a1b940d2b640e5edf0feae90e81bbb6b4941e7/crypto/evp/evp_lib.c#L320-L327

But EVP_MD_block_size and EVP_MD_flags do not:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/64a1b940d2b640e5edf0feae90e81bbb6b4941e7/crypto/evp/evp_lib.c#L305-L308
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/64a1b940d2b640e5edf0feae90e81bbb6b4941e7/crypto/evp/evp_lib.c#L329-L332
